title: The Mediating Role of Resilience in the Association Between Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms Among College Students at a Hispanic-Serving Institution in a U.S.-Mexico Border Region.
abstract: Anxiety and depressive symptoms are prevalent concerns among college students, yet less is known about the role of resilience in their association among students in U.S.-Mexico border regions. This cross-sectional study examined whether resilience statistically mediated the association between anxiety and depressive symptoms while controlling for sociodemographic factors and year of data collection. Participants were a convenience sample of 857 college students attending a Hispanic-serving institution in a U.S.-Mexico border region from 2021 to 2025. Anxiety, resilience, and depressive symptoms were measured using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7, Brief Resilience Scale, and Patient Health Questionnaire-9, respectively. Mediation analysis was conducted using PROCESS Model 4 with 5000 bootstrap samples. Higher anxiety was associated with lower resilience (= -0.056,< 0.001), and greater resilience was associated with lower depressive symptoms (= -1.379,< 0.001). The indirect association of anxiety with depressive symptoms through resilience was significant (= 0.077, 95% bootstrap CI [0.052, 0.103]). The direct association remained significant (= 0.700,< 0.001), indicating partial statistical mediation. These findings suggest that resilience is an important factor in the association between anxiety and depressive symptoms and may inform comprehensive student mental health initiatives.
